sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection of the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" to the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev, emphasizing that the revelation of Chassidus brings about a redemption characterized by peace, without war, through the level of Yechidah.

translations.translation: And according to this, the connection of “He redeemed my soul in peace” etc. will also be understood
[that the emphasis here is that the redemption is specifically in peace]
to the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev
(the revelation of the teachings of Chassidus),
for it is explained in many places
that the essence of the teachings of Chassidus is the revelation of the inner dimension of the Torah,
the innermost aspect of wisdom, the innermost aspect of Abba
(which is the innermost aspect of Atik)
is the level of Yechidah,
and from the perspective of the level of Yechidah, even when there is a state of multiplicity,
the redemption is in peace
(and it can be said that this is even more than the concept of “He makes peace in His high places”
according to the explanation of the Maggid,
which is analogous to the utter nullification of the ministering angel when he comes before the king,
unlike here, where the wills are nullified from the outset),
that there is no need for war at all,
and on the contrary, the service is specifically through pleasant ways and ways of peace,
and through this it is brought about
(as he concludes in the aforementioned Igeres HaKodesh)
that it will be “as water reflects a face,”
that is, as the conclusion of the verse
“so is the heart of man to man,”
and the intention in this is also regarding the level of the Supernal Man,
that there will be the light
of the “face of the King of life,”
that from this there will be
(as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded
on the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace”)
“He redeemed me and my sons from among the nations,”
and this is that very soon “with me is the man, King Moshiach,”
through the service
of “your springs will burst forth”
outwardly,
which primarily began
after the redemption of Yud Tes Kislev,
that out of rest and joy and a good heart, and in a manner of peace, the departure from exile will be in peace, in the true and complete redemption, very soon, from He Who is Peace.
